doctrine: An agent NEVER quarantines a test to make a build green. Adding a row here to
clear a red build is the build-fixing shortcut in its most respectable disguise;
it requires a human author, always. See .flake/README.md.
Every #[ignore] in crates/** must appear in exactly ONE of `quarantine` (a flake,
owned and expiring) or `exempt` (environment-gated, not a flake). Both directions
are checked: `just flake-check` fails on an unregistered ignore AND on a row that
names a test the tree no longer has.
ceilingRationale: Stop-the-line at 5 quarantined tests. The suite has 2039 passing tests and 19
ignores, of which exactly 2 are flakes; a register that reached 5 would mean the
flake rate more than doubled without anyone fixing one, which is the point at
which the suite has quietly stopped certifying timing behaviour at all.

formReason: libtest has no `muted` form: #[ignore] is a skip, so the preferred 'still runs,
result recorded, does not block' shape is not available in-process. The
compensating control is the nightly `long-lanes` CI leg, which runs the whole
--ignored set through scripts/ci/flake-record.mjs — so the outcome history a
mute would have produced accumulates anyway, off the blocking path.
evidence: crates/core/src/governor.rs:340. Asserts a wall-clock lower bound
(`elapsed >= 350ms` for two 200ms per-host gaps) and an upper bound proving 32
hosts did not serialize. The lower bound is sound; the upper bound is what
slips under load, because a loaded machine can serialize the 32 spawned tasks
onto fewer worker threads. Failure signature: `per-host spacing lost` /
the concurrency upper-bound assert, never a logic error in the sharded map.
exitPlan: Replace the wall-clock upper bound with an observation of the sharded map's
own state (per-host next-allowed instants), which is the property the test
actually claims. Wall clock stays only for the lower bound.

formReason: Same as above — #[ignore] is libtest's only form. Staggered a month behind the
governor entry on purpose: two entries expiring on the same day produce one
review that clears both by extension, which is how expiry stops escalating.
evidence: pre-instantiation against per-call relinking. The gate is deliberately
one-sided (pre-instantiation must not be a REGRESSION), but the margin is
small enough that scheduler noise on a shared runner can invert it — the
cause is the harness's resolution, not the product's speed, which is why this
exitPlan: Take the best-of-N per path rather than the total of N, so a single descheduled
iteration cannot decide the comparison; release once the nightly lane shows a
full 14-day window with no outcome transition.
